content:
maria_ml: quick heads-up — saw a ~2.4% EM drop on qa-bench when serving AWQ-INT8 with prefix cache + continuous batching on. anyone else run into this?
kevin_infra: uhoh. what infra + batcher config? could be batching window interacting with cache hits.
carla_eval: pasted the numbers from the run I grabbed:
```
model: rw-gpt-13b-like
quant: awq-int8
dataset: qa-bench (dev)
baseline fp16 EM: 78.6
awq-int8 (no cache, no contbatch) EM: 76.2  (-2.4)
awq-int8 + prefix-cache EM: 74.1  (-4.5 vs fp16)
awq-int8 + prefix-cache + continuous-batching EM: 73.7  (-4.9)
perplexity fp16: 12.1 -> awq-int8: 12.9
```
carla_eval: config bits: batcher.max_batch_tokens=512, batcher.batch_window_ms=10, continuous_batching=true, cache.prefix.enabled=true, cache.max_prefix_len=128
maria_ml: note — this was on mixed prompt lengths (short chat prompts + long context docs).
dan_oncall: also saw tail latency creep: p90 280ms -> 360ms with contbatch + cache, p99 spikes more variable. looks like batching is waiting for cache hits/invalidations? :thinking: 
kevin_infra: hypothesis: prefix cache causes more KV cache hits that change effective token counts per request, so the batcher mis-estimates batch size and delays. continuous batching then exacerbates by holding small requests to assemble larger batches, increasing chance of stale cache state or alignment?
eva_prod: quick mitigation: try setting cache.min_prefix_len=32 or disable prefix cache for queries < 64 tokens, and lower batch_window_ms to 6 for the canary.
carla_eval: tried cache.min_prefix_len=64 + batch_window_ms=6 in a small canary — EM improved back to 75.1 (still ~1.5% down vs fp16) but latency regained.
quant-bot: experiment summary: run_id=exp/2027-03-02-az1-042, artifacts: s3://redwood-inference/experiments/exp-1802504321 (logs, configs, eval.json) :white_check_mark:
maria_ml: nice. next steps: 1) reproduce under deterministic workload (all-short queries) 2) run AWQ int8 with per-channel scaling variant 3) try GPTQ run w/ same batching/cache config for comparison
kevin_infra: also add telemetry: per-request cache_hit boolean + batch_size_at_send to trace. that'll let us see correlations.
dan_oncall: FYI filed incident ticket INC-2027-089 to track canary and rollback policy if production sees >2% regression.
eva_prod: canary rollout plan: 5% traffic AWQ-int8 w/ cache disabled for short queries, monitor EM+latency for 24h, then 20% with cache on and batch_window tweak.
carla_eval: for repro, run this locally:
```
python eval/run_eval.py --model awq-int8 --cache-prefix 64 --batch-window-ms 8 --dataset qa-bench --out run_awq_cache.json
```
carla_eval: also attach eval prompt set that triggered biggest delta: short-question-with-long-context-001.json
maria_ml: thanks — I'll kick off the deterministic runs, tagging you all. @carla_eval please upload the prompt set to the experiment dir. :eyes:
kevin_infra: added trace fields to batcher yesterday, should be live for the next canary.
quant-bot: scheduled follow-up: auto-compare AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP16 for new run_id=exp/1802504789 in 2h.
maria_ml: perfect. if we still see gap after tuning cache/batcher, we'll consider a light quant-aware fine-tune or switching quant kernel.
